display.purpose: Masthead name only. One per page.

headline.purpose: Section h2 (Position, Record, Ask the resume, Colophon). Set tight.

title.purpose: Listing role names, project entry names, callout titles inside listing blocks.

body.purpose: Prose copy. IBM Plex Serif, full ink, capped at 60–70ch measure.

label.purpose: Eyebrows, group labels, recordation stamps, mono metadata. The Plex Mono voice.

motion.name: ease-state
motion.purpose: Default transition for color and border-color state changes (hover, focus). Short, no overshoot.

narrative.overview: The site is a 1960s real-estate listing office, transposed to a senior engineer's portfolio. The page reads as a platted document with five lettered sections (§ 01 Masthead, § 02 Position, § 03 Record, § 04 Working artifact, § 05 Colophon). Every entry is filed, dated, stamped. Type carries hierarchy; color punctuates. The voice is considered, exact, dry. The system rejects the SaaS / Vercel-template default (cream ground, gradient blob hero, three-card feature grid, Inter-everywhere typography). Cream is substituted for cool monochrome-tint Slate Mist to escape the warm-on-warm archival-editorial reflex. Inter is rejected for IBM Plex Serif as the body face. The signature gesture is the Enamel Mark — a 6–8px Cordovan square that recurs as a load-bearing indicator across the system.
keyCharacteristics: Type carries hierarchy; color punctuates ≤10% of any given screen.
Single committed light theme. No dark mode. The Slate Mist ground is the brand decision.
Hairline-only rounding: 0px (display, marks, masthead) and 2px (buttons, tinted surfaces). No SaaS-default 8–12px radii.
Real-estate-listing register: listing block, plat rule, enamel mark, recordation stamp are the four signature motifs.
IBM Plex three-voice: Sans Condensed (display), Serif (body, anchoring the editorial register), Mono (eyebrows, metadata, code).
Motion budget: state transitions only (120ms ease-out). No scroll choreography, no parallax, no autoplay, no 'wow on load.'

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Cordovan is the single committed accent. It carries CTAs, links, the Enamel Mark, and current-state indicators. No second saturated accent enters the system. Vermilion is its hover, not a peer.

rules.name: The Cool-Ground Rule
rules.body: The page ground is cool monochrome-tint, never cream or any cream rebrand (vellum, kami, bone, ivory, eggshell, oatmeal). The cream-ground default is the editorial-archival reflex this brand explicitly rejects.

rules.name: The Punctuation Rule
rules.body: Color punctuates ≤10% of pixel surface. If color reaches 30%+, something is wrong with the typesetting. Restraint as competence signal.

rules.name: The Warm-Cool Inversion Rule
rules.body: Warm-saturated accents sit on a cool-neutral ground. Never invert this — warm ground with warm accents collapses into the archival-editorial default.

rules.name: The Body-Serif Rule
rules.body: Body sets in Plex Serif, never Plex Sans. The serif anchor pulls the site out of the saturated 'developer-who-picked-Inter' lane. This is the single most load-bearing typographic decision in the system.

rules.name: The Mono-Reserved Rule
rules.body: Plex Mono is for metadata, eyebrows, recordation stamps, and code only. Mono-as-body is on the watch list ('developer who just discovered IBM Plex Mono').

rules.name: The No-Em-Dash Rule
rules.body: Em dashes are not used in copy. Year ranges use en dashes. Sentence interruptions use commas, colons, semicolons, parentheses. Also not '--'.

rules.name: The Italic-One-Word Rule
rules.body: Italic accent is one word per heading at most; usually zero. Italic is for actual emphasis, not decoration.

rules.name: The Tabular-Numerals Rule
rules.body: Numerals are tabular in tables, listings, and metadata; proportional in prose.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. No box-shadow. The chat frame and recognition block lift off ground via Plat Deep tint, not via shadow.

rules.name: The Plat-Rule Rule
rules.body: Horizontal rules are the divider vocabulary. They use rgba ink at 18% (rule) for fine subdivisions and 55% (rule-strong) for major section borders. Never thicker than 1px. Never in saturated color.

dos: Do carry the Enamel Mark consistently as a load-bearing indicator. It marks meaning (current, primary, latest), never decoration.
Do use Plex Serif for body. The serif is the anchor that pulls the site out of the 'developer who picked Inter' lane.
Do name systems precisely in copy. 'A queue' becomes 'a Cloudflare Queue with a 30-second visibility window.' Specificity is the dominant rhetorical move.
Do use full ink for body text. Opacity-softened body (e.g., body at 65%) is on the watch list.
Do keep year ranges in en dashes (2022–Present), not em dashes or hyphens.
Do lift surfaces via Plat Deep tint, never via box-shadow.
Do use tabular numerals in listings and tables; proportional in prose.
Do verify every claim names the system, the constraint, or the number that backs it up.
donts: Don't use cream or any cream rebrand (vellum, kami, bone, ivory, eggshell, oatmeal, parchment, washi, biscuit) as the page ground. The Slate Mist ground is committed.
Don't use Inter, Helvetica Neue, or any neutral grotesque as the primary face. IBM Plex is the brand commitment.
Don't add gradient backgrounds, glassmorphism, blur effects, or background-clip: text gradient text. All on the absolute ban list.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored stripe accent. Side-stripe borders are an absolute ban.
Don't add the hero-metric template (big number + small label + supporting stats + gradient accent). SaaS cliché.
Don't stack identical card grids. Three identical icon+heading+text cards in a row is a watch-list pattern.
Don't ship dark mode without a designed dark variant. Single-mode commitment is the brand decision.
Don't add scroll choreography, parallax, autoplay video, or 'wow on load' animations.
Don't use exclamation points outside of quoted speech.
Don't use em dashes in copy.
Don't use marketing adjectives: artisanal, crafted, premium, curated, beloved, cozy, warm, inviting, thoughtfully, delightfully, lovingly, uncompromising, bespoke, leveraging, passionate.
Don't invent 'Tools' or 'Skills' walls. Logo grids of every tool are an explicit anti-reference.
Don't add a floating 'Talk to me' FAB. The colophon CTA + masthead email is sufficient.

Don't soften the 'first production' claim back to 'the first production.' The line is 'one of the first production AEM Edge Delivery Services plus Adobe Commerce B2B integrations.' Specificity is honesty.
Don't add sticky bottom CTAs, intercom-style chat bubbles, or banner cookie consents that violate the document register.
Don't rename the six DESIGN.md sections.
